rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the certificate's subject public-key algorithm together with its key size or curve, as a `VARCHAR` built by this worker (not Go's bare algorithm name). The value follows a fixed convention: RSA keys render as `RSA-<bits>` where <bits> is the modulus size, typically `RSA-2048`, `RSA-3072` or `RSA-4096`; ECDSA keys render as `ECDSA-<curve>` with the curve name stripped of its hyphen, i.e. `ECDSA-P256`, `ECDSA-P384`, `ECDSA-P521`; Edwards keys render as the single token `Ed25519`, and X25519, X448 and Ed448 keys as `X25519`, `X448`, `Ed448`. Any other key type Go recognises falls back to Go's public-key algorithm name (e.g. `DSA`, `ML-DSA`); an unrecognised key algorithm yields `Unknown`. For a security audit, RSA moduli below 2048 bits are considered weak. Accepts PEM text (`VARCHAR`) or DER bytes (`BLOB`); NULL input yields NULL. Example: the committed fixture certificate carries a P-256 ECDSA key and returns `ECDSA-P256`.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the algorithm the issuing CA used to sign this certificate, as a `VARCHAR`. The value is Go crypto/x509's canonical name for the algorithm and is drawn from a fixed vocabulary: for RSA PKCS#1 v1.5, `SHA256-RSA`, `SHA384-RSA`, `SHA512-RSA` (and the legacy `SHA1-RSA`, `MD5-RSA`); for RSA-PSS, `SHA256-RSAPSS`, `SHA384-RSAPSS`, `SHA512-RSAPSS`; for ECDSA, `ECDSA-SHA256`, `ECDSA-SHA384`, `ECDSA-SHA512` (and legacy `ECDSA-SHA1`); for DSA, `DSA-SHA1`, `DSA-SHA256`; `Ed25519`; and `ML-DSA-44`, `ML-DSA-65`, `ML-DSA-87`. An unrecognised OID, including the obsolete MD2-RSA, yields `Unknown`. Note the ordering convention differs by family — RSA/DSA render as hash-then-key (`SHA256-RSA`) while ECDSA renders as key-then-hash (`ECDSA-SHA256`) — so match on the whole token, not a positional split. For a security audit, the SHA-1 and MD5 variants (and `Unknown`) are considered weak/deprecated and are the ones worth flagging. Accepts PEM text (`VARCHAR`) or DER bytes (`BLOB`); NULL input yields NULL. Example: the committed fixture certificate is P-256 ECDSA and returns `ECDSA-SHA256`.
